author: Penry Buckley
description:
Son of former ABC chair will contest seat of Cessnock in March state election and says ‘my wife’s Japanese’ so he doesn’t believe party is racist

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation has named investment banker Mike Newman as its New South Wales leader and first lower house candidate ahead of the March 2027 state election.

Pauline Hanson was to hold a press conference alongside Newman on Friday morning to announce the son of former
title: One Nation’s new NSW leader Mike Newman is an investment banker who wants to ‘get rid of wokery’

author: Robert Mackey
description:
Three employees of Stars and Stripes, a government-funded news service, allege they were fired after reporting on USS Abraham Lincoln

Three journalists who were fired by the Pentagon from a US government-funded news outlet sued the Department of Defense in federal court on Thursday, arguing their dismissals were illegal and violated their first amendment rights to free speech.

The three journalists were all employees of Stars and Stripes, which their court filing calls “the U.S. military’s independent news source since the Civil War with a long history of editorial independence, free from news management or censorship by military command”.
title: Three journalists sue Pentagon after being fired from military news outlet

author: Rupert Jones
description:
New rules are aimed at protecting people in debt in England and Wales and stopping homeowners being ripped off

A clampdown on “rogue bailiffs” has been launched by Andy Burnham amid concerns that vulnerable people are being overcharged and face aggressive behaviour.

In the latest in a series of “everyday fixes” to ease the cost of living and “make Britain fairer”, the prime minister said he was strengthening the rules that apply to bailiffs in England and Wales to better protect people in debt.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham announces crackdown on rogue bailiffs and ‘cowboy builders’

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Foreign affairs minister Penny Wong confirms increase to number of Australians missing

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Voluntary assisted dying laws have been passed in the Northern Territory jurisdiction following debate over a gag clause barring doctors from raising end-of-life options with patients, Australian Associated Press reports.

The rights of the terminally ill bill passed on a conscience vote in the Northern Territory parliament late last night, with the gag intact.

Continue reading...
title: Australia news live: number of Australians missing in Nepal increases to 39; voluntary assisted dying now legal nation-wide

author: Anna Betts
description:
Grand jury declined to indict anyone but said there was a ‘sophisticated scheme’ to use funds for political activity

  • US politics live – latest updates

A Florida grand jury has found that the administration of the governor, Ron DeSantis, “misappropriated” $10m in taxpayer money from a Medicaid settlement into the Hope Florida Foundation, a charity with ties to DeSantis’s wife, before the money was reportedly “funneled” into “two political action committees”.

In the
title: Florida grand jury finds DeSantis administration ‘misappropriated’ funds from Medicaid settlement

author: Shrai Popat in Washington
description:
Congressman Jamie Raskin asks president’s son to detail firm’s recent success after he joined 1798 Capital as partner

Democrats on a powerful US congressional committee have launched an investigation into a venture capital firm which has thrived since recruiting Donald Trump’s son.

Donald Trump Jr joined 1798 Capital as a partner just days after his father won a second term in office in November 2024. Congressman Jamie Raskin, ranking member of the US House of Representatives judiciary committee, has asked the president’s son to detail the firm’s recent success.

Continue reading...
title: Democrats to investigate ‘miraculous’ rise of Trump Jr’s investment firm

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Representative Mike Collins has been dogged by associations to white nationalism and antisemitism

  • US politics live – latest updates

The US senator for Georgia Jon Ossoff, a Democrat, has slammed a “disgraceful and disqualifying” report that a former staffer for his Trump-backed Republican challenger Mike Collins shared images online of a swastika and depicting himself in Ku Klux Klan robes.

It is the latest instance of someone in Collins’s orbit facing scrutiny over racist or white nationalist conduct. Ossoff called the report “stunning” and said it “should shock the conscience of every Georgian”.

Continue reading...
title: Georgia senator Jon Ossoff slams racist posts allegedly from Republican opponent’s ex-staffer

author: Nadeem Badshah
description:
Montreal-born actor also voiced KARR in Knight Rider and the monster in Predator, having started his career on Canadian TV and radio

Peter Cullen, the actor behind the voice of characters including Eeyore in Disney’s Winnie the Pooh franchise and Optimus Prime in Transformers, has died aged 85.

He died on Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles, a statement said.

Continue reading...
title: Actor Peter Cullen, voice of Optimus Prime and Eeyore, dies aged 85

author: Kiran StaceyPolicy editor
description:
Exclusive: Campaigners accuse prime minister of U-turn after he decided not to back funding cap in elections bill

Andy Burnham recently supported an even lower donations cap than previously reported, according to correspondence seen by the Guardian, as the row over next week’s elections bill escalates.

The prime minister wrote to a campaigner in May outlining his support for a £500,000 individual donations cap, which he said would “guard against the perception of any one party being unduly influenced or swayed by one person or organisation”.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham recently suggested £500k political donation cap that would be ‘reduced over time’

author: Jonathan Watts
description:
Unusual heat this year may have melted ice and thawed bonds that hold glaciers in place – leading to catastrophe

  • Nepal-Tibet flash flood – latest updates

  • What caused the flash flood in Nepal and Tibet?

The devastating flash flood that has ripped through the border communities of Nepal and Tibet has heightened fears that the climate crisis is destabilising the geology of mountain and polar regions, threatening millions of people.

Satellite imagery suggests a glacier collapse high in the Himalayas was the primary cause of the deadly torrent of mud, water and ice that tore along the Bhotekoshi River on Wednesday. It swept
title: Climate crisis could be destabilising mountain areas like Nepal, experts warn

author: Oliver Milman
description:
‘Godzilla’ event currently brewing could push 50 million people into acute hunger before the end of next year

A series of strong El Niño climatic patterns in recent decades, such as the “Godzilla” event currently brewing that is set to warp weather around the world, have been supercharged by the broader overheating of the planet caused by the burning of fossil fuels, a major new study has found.

El Niño is a naturally occurring phenomenon, taking place every two to seven years, when the waters of the eastern tropical Pacific Ocean heat up, causing a cascade of impacts around the world. The latest developing El Niño, set to peak later this year, is set to be the strongest in living memory and has been informally dubbed a “Godzilla” event.

Continue r
title: El Niño climate patterns supercharged by burning of fossil fuels, study finds

author: George Chidi
description:
Symbolic move to rename lake bordering New York and Canada comes amid escalating trade war with northern neighbor

  • US politics live – latest updates

Donald Trump signed an executive order on Thursday directing the federal government to rename Lake Ontario, making it Lake America.

The largely symbolic move comes amid an escalating trade war with Canada.

Continue reading...
title: Trump signs executive order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America

author: Caroline Davies and agency
description:
Sally-Anne Bowen, now 65, convicted of assaulting boys at Christ’s College, Finchley, where she was chemistry teacher

A chemistry teacher has been found guilty of indecently assaulting two teenage pupils at an all-boys school in the late 1980s.

Sally-Anne Bowen, who taught at Christ’s College in Finchley, north London, assaulted the teenage boys when they were aged around 14 to 15 and she was in her mid-20s.

Continue reading...
title: Woman found guilty of indecent assault against two pupils at London boys’ school in 1980s

author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
description:
Jes Staley made the comments to US lawmakers investigating his links to Jeffrey Epstein

The former Barclays boss Jes Staley has denied having sex with a woman dressed as Snow White, after being questioned about an infamous email exchange about Disney princesses with Jeffrey Epstein.

The comments were detailed in newly released transcripts from a closed-door interview last month with US lawmakers as part of their investigation into Epstein, who died in prison in August 2019 while awaiting trial on child sex-trafficking charges.

Continue reading...
title: Ex-Barclays boss denies having sex with a woman dressed as Snow White

author: Aram Roston
description:
Exclusive: Experts and former officials say accounts are running dry, and funding a war with no clear endgame is the main challenge

Donald Trump’s war on Iran has driven the US military into a severe financial crisis, with the US navy forced to transfer money from its payroll and other sources to cover the costs of combat, according to documents obtained by the Guardian, and interviews with navy officials, contractors and defense analysts.

The US-Israeli operation, which has depleted US munitions stockpiles and prompted retaliatory Iranian strikes that have wrecked strategic bases across the Middle East, is piling pressure on budgets across the military.

Continue reading...
title: Trump’s war on Iran is rapidly draining US navy budget, documents and interviews reveal

author: Maya Yangand agencies
description:
The state concludes: ‘This wasn’t a woman suffering from a lack of care’ or ‘a lack of resources’

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

The jury in the Lindsay Clancy trial has moved into deliberations as jurors decide whether the 36-year-old former labor and delivery nurse is criminally responsible for fatally strangling her three children in January 2023.

Over the past five weeks, the trial, which has been called “America’s saddest murder trial” , has renewed nationwide atten
title: Jury deliberations begin in Lindsay Clancy murder trial after her attorney blames medical system

author: Philip Oltermann European culture editor
description:
Father Dionysios Tabakis says his views are those of the Orthodox church ‘nothing more, nothing less’

A Greek Orthodox priest whose home-recorded album of drone metal and religious dubstep has made him a cult figure in experimental music circles has issued a statement in which he has clarified his stance on homosexuality and the Greek radical right.

“As can be seen from my musical expression, I am in favour of unity, love, empathy and help for every needy, wronged and suffering person in life,” Father Dionysios Tabakis said in a public statement shared with the Guardian. “Whoever they are, whatever they believe, whether they are a saint or a sinner.”

Continue reading...
title: Greek Orthodox priest and cult musician clarifies views on homosexuality

author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
description:
Labour’s Andy McDonald says gangs ‘clearly featuring’ in a series of incidents and police are underfunded

Five MPs on Teesside have called on the government to provide more help to local police and fire services after a week in which nine people have died in two incidents.

The MPs said the communities they represented should get the “strongest possible backing from the government”.

Continue reading...
title: Teesside MPs call for more police help after Middlesbrough and A66 deaths

author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Gaurav Pokharel in Kathmandu, Sam Jones and Amy Hawkins
description:
Flash floods have killed at least 359 people while homes and infrastructure have been swept away

  • Nepal-Tibet flash flood – latest updates

  • What caused the flash flood in Nepal and Tibet?

The international community was scrambling to get aid into flood-stricken parts of Nepal and Tibet on Thursday as authorities warned that a lake ⁠formed at the ⁠site ⁠where the ​deadly torrents occurred ⁠was rising and ⁠at risk ​of ‌bursting.

The catastrophic flash floods that hit Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday, thundering down valleys and obliterating entire villages, killed at least 359 people and left more than 1,300 missing.
title: Race to get aid into Nepal and Tibet amid warnings flood lake could burst

author: Reuters
description:
Andrew and Tristan Tate’s lawyer tells court that pair, who are wanted on rape charges, are not a flight risk

A lawyer for the social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate urged a US judge on Thursday to release the brothers on bail from a Miami jail ⁠as they contest extradition to Britain, ⁠where they are wanted ​on rape charges.

Howard Srebnick, a lawyer for the Tate brothers, told the Miami-based US magistrate judge Lauren Louis that they had regularly appeared in court in Romania, where they are on pre-trial release, which he said ⁠was evidence they were not a flight risk.

Continue reading...
title: Tate brothers urge release on bail in Miami as they fight extradition to UK

author: George Chidi
description:
Move from USPS comes amid Trump administration’s efforts to restrict mail-in voting in November’s midterms

The US Postal Service (USPS) said on ​Thursday ‌that ‌new ‌requirements for mail-in ‌voting are ​now ⁠in effect as Donald Trump seeks to crack down on the practice. The move is expected to trigger a new round of legal challenges.

The Trump administration has sought to impose new rules requiring state election leaders to submit their voter rolls for inspection as part of a broader bid to increase federal government oversight over voting and elections.

Continue reading...
title: US Postal Service says new mail ballot rules tied to Trump order are in effect

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Judge ruled Jeanine John Taele, discovered with firearm days before Trump visit, was unfit to face felony charge

A judge in California has suspended criminal proceedings against a man found with a loaded gun near Donald Trump’s golf course in Los Angeles, and instead ordered him to undergo a mental health evaluation.

Jeanine John Taele, 38, of Downey, California, was arrested for weapons violations days before the president spoke at a 5 August Republican fundraiser at the Trump National Golf Club in Rancho Palos Verdes.

Continue reading...
title: Judge orders mental health evaluation for man found with gun at Trump golf course in LA

author: Jessica Elgot, Diane Taylor and Chris Osuh
description:
Small boat crossings also down 23% year-on-year, with Home Office citing more trafficking arrests

  • UK politics live – latest updates

The number of asylum seekers living in hotels has halved within a year, including 13 closures over the past month alone, according to new migration statistics.

Sweeping changes to the asylum system have also seen a significant drop in legal arrivals and asylum claims. But the numbers of asylum seekers who are now being housed in private accommodation has increased, as the government shifts numbers being housed in hotels into privately rented houses in multiple occupation (HMOs).

Continue reading...
title: Number of asylum seekers living in hotels across UK halves within a year

author: Kate Connolly in Berlin
description:
Mosquito traps are set up at Germany’s biggest airport, with doctors told to watch for symptoms of deadly disease

German health officials are seeking to reassure the public after two workers at the country’s biggest airport died of malaria.

Mosquito traps have been set up at Frankfurt airport and a mosquito monitoring process is under way. A detailed investigation is being conducted to clarify how the workers contracted the disease.

Continue reading...
title: Officials urge calm after malaria outbreak kills two staff at Frankfurt airport

author: Anna Betts
description:
Thai navy says ‘routine’ visit’ will allow personnel to rest and recuperate amid reports of poor conditions onboard

The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier is set to make a temporary stop in Thailand next week as it heads back to the United States, Thai navy officials said, after spending more than 250 consecutive days at sea supporting US operations against Iran amid recent reports of poor living conditions and low morale onboard the vessel.

The Lincoln left the Middle East several days ago after being relieved by the USS George Washington, and is now heading
title: USS Abraham Lincoln to visit port in Thailand after more than 250 days at sea

author: Sarah Basford Canales
description:
The party’s key figures are either unable or unwilling to neatly articulate their migration targets, contradicting one another – and themselves

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation has experienced a swell in popular support in the past year, and has primarily done so off the back of tough talk on immigration – a policy area almost synonymous with its leader, Pauline Hanson.

But a series of blunders this week show a party unable, or unwilling, to clearly articulate what it would actually do about immigration levels.

Continue reading...
title: One Nation’s immigration policy is clear as mud – but that ambiguity could be a secret weapon for Pauline Hanson

author: Evan Simon of Floodlight
description:
Thermal drone footage shows a Microsoft-backed AI datacenter powering its operations with dozens of unpermitted generators

The largest planned AI datacenter in New Jersey is being accused of violating federal law after a visual investigation found the site running dozens of unpermitted gas-powered generators.

Thermal drone footage captured by the non-profit newsroom Floodlight last week showed the partly completed DataOne facility in Vineland was operating at least 45 of the site’s 62 generators at the time.

Continue reading...
title: One of east coast’s largest datacenters accused of ‘violating federal law’

author: Presented by Kiran Stacey and Peter Walker, produced by Ned Carter Miles, music by Axel Kacoutié; the executive producer was Frankie Tobi
description:
It’s been a month since Andy Burnham became prime minister. And while polls have shown a ‘Burnham bounce’, the coming months will force the new PM into making some tough – and potentially unpopular – decisions that will reveal how serious he is about delivering the changes he believes the country needs. Kiran Stacey and Peter Walker look at the choices facing Burnham

Please keep sending your comments and questions to Pippa and Kiran at politicsweeklyuk@theguardian.com.

Listen back to Kiran’s interview with Bridget Phillipson here

And, read Kiran’s article about possible changes to Insolvency Law here
title: Andy Burnham’s autumn of pain– podcast

author: Peter Beaumont Senior international correspondent
description:
Bosnian Serb commander responsible for Srebrenica massacre dies in prison while serving life sentence for genocide

Ratko Mladić, the infamous Serbian general who was serving a life sentence for genocide committed during the Bosnian war, has died in prison in the Hague, a UN official and his lawyer confirmed.

Mladić, 84, had been one of the main architects of the policy of ethnic cleansing during the Bosnian war. He was convicted of genocide for orchestrating the 1995 killing of at least 8,000 Muslims in the UN-designated “safe area” Srebrenica, the worst massacre in Europe since the second world war.

Continue reading...
title: Ratko Mladić, the ‘Butcher of Bosnia’, dies aged 84

author: Associated Press
description:
Judge rules Christian Castro, accused of shooting man and lying about it, cannot be held pending extradition request

An Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer charged with shooting a man and lying about it during the immigration crackdown in Minneapolis was released from a Texas jail on Thursday, after a judge refused to order his return to Minnesota.

Christian Castro was released at the break of dawn from a detention center in Brownsville. He motioned his hand toward a few camera operators and a reporter crowding around him and quickly got into an SUV that drove off.

Continue reading...
title: ICE agent charged with Minnesota shooting released from jail in Texas

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Adam Kalkstein compared administration’s order to ‘trying to teach the law’ without mentioning ‘the constitution’

The only climate scientist teaching at West Point, the US army’s military academy, was fired after he resisted an order to stop teaching about the human causes of the climate emergency, a lawsuit claims.

Dr Adam Kalkstein, a civilian professor of geography at the New York institution, was terminated after the spring semester this year, six months after a testy meeting with Brig Gen Shane Reeves, then dean of West Point’s academic board, the court filing said.

Continue reading...
title: West Point’s only climate scientist fired after continuing to teach human causes of climate change

author: Sarah Butler
description:
First robot-assisted outlet opens in Liverpool to take on Shein and supermarkets in clothing, shoes and homewares

  • Business live – latest updates

The owner of Zara is taking on Primark, Shein and the supermarkets with the launch of its cut-price chain Lefties in Britain, backed by an army of robots.

The Spanish fashion brand opened its first UK store in Liverpool on Thursday, a few weeks after quietly launching its UK website.

Continue reading...
title: Bots and bargains: Zara owner launches cut-price Lefties in UK to rival Primark

author: Andrew Gregory Health editor in Munich
description:
Experts say findings mean breast screenings for cancer could also flag cardiovascular problems in women

Doctors have discovered a way to use routine mammograms that screen for breast cancer to spot heart disease, the world’s leading – and frequently underdiagnosed – cause of death in women.

Researchers analysed the scans using artificial intelligence and were able to successfully identify women with coronary heart disease, high blood pressure or who had suffered a stroke.

Continue reading...
title: AI can detect heart disease in women using mammograms, study suggests

author: Angela Giuffrida in Rome
description:
Bag, camera and pipe belonging to 86-year-old are latest relics uncovered as glaciers melt due to global heating

An 86-year-old mountaineer has been reunited with his backpack and climbing equipment after they emerged from a melting glacier in Austria – more than 60 years after he was forced to leave them there.

Items including an ice axe, camera and a pipe dating from the 1950s or 1960s were discovered on the Sulztalferner glacier in Austria’s Tyrol region, at an altitude of 2,955 metres (9,700ft) above sea level, by a hiker in July.

Continue reading...
title: Hiker reunited with backpack 60 years after he fell into a glacier in Austria

author: Philip Oltermann and agencies
description:
Gold collection known as Treasure of Villena, worth at least €1.7m, is latest target of criminal raid

Thieves in Spain have raided the Treasure of Villena – a stunning collection of bronze age gold artefacts that has been described as the most important prehistoric trove in Europe – in the latest high-profile smash-and-grab heist on the continent.

The raid on Thursday morning of the 66 mostly gold objects in the Spanish town of Villena lasted just minutes, officials said.

Continue reading...
title: Thieves steal bronze age treasure in ‘very well planned’ four-minute museum heist in Spain

author: Kevin Rawlinson and agency
description:
Coroner is told BBC veteran was dazzled by headlights before collision and her injuries led to bronchopneumonia

The broadcaster Jenni Murray died days after being involved in a car crash that happened when she was dazzled by headlights, a coroner has heard.

Murray, 75, was best known as the voice of BBC Radio 4’s Woman’s Hour, hosting the programme for three decades and becoming the longest-serving presenter in its history.

Continue reading...
title: Broadcaster Jenni Murray died days after north London car crash, inquest hears

author: Caroline Davies
description:
Motoring series to return four years after Andrew ‘Freddie’ Flintoff suffered serious injuries in crash during filming

Top Gear, the long-running motoring show that has been off air since its co-host Andrew “Freddie” Flintoff was seriously injured in a crash during filming almost four years ago, is to return to the BBC, the broadcaster confirmed today.

After Flintoff’s accident at Dunsfold aerodrome in Surrey, the BBC said the series would be “rested” for the foreseeable future.

Continue reading...
title: BBC to bring back Top Gear amid speculation about show’s next presenters

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Company that runs Manchester, Stansted and East Midlands hubs says passenger safety is unaffected

  • Business live – latest updates

Manchester, London Stansted and East Midlands airports have been hit by a cyber-attack, with hackers accessing the data of about 8.7 million customers.

Hackers obtained their email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registration numbers and postcodes, as the incident affected data related to “car park, lounge and fast-track bookings and in-airport wifi sign-ups”, said Manchester Airports Group (MAG), which operates the three air hubs.

Continue reading...
title: Three UK airports hit by cyber-attack with data of 8.7m customers accessed

author: Guardian staff
description:
Earth’s shadow will appear to be a reddish ‘blood moon’ due to the way sunlight is scattered by the atmosphere

A near total lunar eclipse will be visible across large swathes of North and South America on Thursday night with millions of people expected to be able to see one of nature’s marvels.

Lunar eclipses occur when Earth moves between the sun and the moon and its shadow is cast on to the lunar surface. Thursday night’s event will see 96% of the moon darkened by the Earth’s shadow at its peak moment.

Continue reading...
title: Near total lunar eclipse will be seen from North and South America Thursday night

author: Michelle R Smith
description:
Letters obtained by Guardian and AP contradict testimony that 2019 visit to Samoa had ‘nothing to do with vaccines’

Newly obtained documents indicate that the US health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, lied during two congressional hearings last year, telling lawmakers who held the key to his confirmation that a 2019 visit to Samoa had “nothing to do with vaccines”.

Letters obtained by the Guardian and the Associated Press contradict that testimony. In one he wrote to the Samoan prime minister before the trip, Kennedy explicitly said he wanted to study the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine in the Pacific island nation. In it, he used the words vaccine or vaccination eight times.

Continue reading...
title: RFK Jr lied in Senate confirmation hearings, newly revealed documents indicate

author: Associated Press
description:
Plane was headed for airport in Seldovia from Anchorage, and was submerged in water after the crash

A small plane carrying four people crashed into shallow waters next to a remote coastal town in Alaska on Wednesday, killing everyone on board, according to officials.

The Piper PA-24 was headed for the airport in the small town of Seldovia after taking off from Anchorage, according to a statement from the Alaska Department of Public Safety. Seldovia’s airport is about 136 miles (219 km) south-west of Anchorage.

Continue reading...
title: Plane headed for remote Alaska town crashes and kills all four passengers on board

author: Peter Beaumont, senior international correspondent
description:
Kremlin threatens retaliation after Burnham says UK will help Ukraine start producing long-range missiles

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Russia has said it could retaliate against the UK for its support of Kyiv by striking military targets inside and outside Ukraine, amid reports that the director of the CIA warned the Kremlin against attacking Nato during a secretive visit this week.

Andy Burnham, Britain’s prime minister, said on Monday the UK would allow Kyiv access to classified technology to start ⁠its own production of Storm Shadow ​long-range ​cruise missiles. Maria ⁠Zakharova, Russia’s foreign ministry spokesperson, said on Thursday Britain and France were
title: Russia warns Britain is ‘playing with fire’ over its support of Ukraine

author: Martin Belam
description:
Safety features including usage limits and night-time blocks to be set by default. Plus changes to famous French cheeses

Good morning. Meta has agreed to significant changes to its Instagram and Facebook apps in a settlement that ended a landmark lawsuit. The agreement curtails a major trial in California and will require the social media company to pay up to $18bn. Meta agreed to establish safeguards for teenage users, including daily usage limits and blocks on night-time use nationwide in the US.

California and 28 other US states sued the $1.36tn (£1tn) company over allegations that Meta deliberately designed addictive products that hooked young people, leading to mental health issues, including anxiety, depression and suicide. As part of the settlement, the company denies wrongdoing.

What will be changing in the apps? The biggest altera
title: First Thing: Meta agrees to make sweeping changes to apps for teens | Martin Belam

author: Neha Gohil Midlands correspondent
description:
City residents had accused council of giving ‘free rein’ to campaign promoting England flags

Birmingham city council is seeking an injunction to stop members of an anti-migrant group from erecting flags, including union jack and St George’s flags, on public infrastructure across the city.

A nationwide campaign to give prominence to the England flag, which resulted in thousands of St George’s crosses being flown from lamp-posts, roundabouts and other public infrastructure, is believed to have started last summer in Birmingham.

Continue reading...
title: Birmingham seeks injunction to stop anti-migrant group erecting flags on infrastructure

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Analysis by Institute for Policy Studies found that between 2019 and 2025, CEO compensation increased 41.4%

The average CEO of the US’s 100 largest, lowest-paying corporations earned 614 times more than their average worker last year, according to an analysis by the Institute for Policy Studies (IPS).

IPS’s latest executive excess report analyzed compensation at the 100 S&P 500 corporations with the lowest median worker pay. Between 2019 and 2025, CEO compensation increased 41.4%, unadjusted for inflation, twice as much as the median worker pay increased at these firms during the same period, at 20.7%.

Continue reading...
title: CEOs earn 614 times more than workers at US’s 100 lowest-paying corporations

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Kremlin dismisses US media reports after meeting as ‘scare stories’, as Pentagon policy chief prepares to meet Nato secretary general

China’s foreign minister said his country and the United States should overcome obstacles between the nations ahead of an expected summit next month between the US president, Donald Trump, and the Chinese president, Xi Jinping.

Wang Yi met the US ambassador to China, David Perdue, on Wednesday and called on both sides to “focus on the positive agenda, properly manage differences, remove interference and overcome obstacles to high-level exchanges between the two countries”, the Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: CIA chief reportedly warns Russia against attacking Nato countries on visit to Moscow – US politics live

author: Phillip Inman
description:
Number of Neets is 30,000 higher than a year ago but figures boost efforts to reverse rise in economic inactivity

The number of young people not in education, employment or training (Neet) across the UK fell below 1 million in the latest three-month period.

In a boost to the government’s efforts to reverse years of rising economic inactivity among people aged 16 to 24, the Office for National Statistics said its surveys showed there were an estimated 981,000 Neets in April to June, compared with 1,012,000 in January to March.

On an annual basis, the number of Neets was 30,000 higher than a year ago, but the fall covering the most recent three-month period will give a lift to ministers concerned that, at 13%, the proportion of young people outside work, education and training remains among the highest in Europe.

Continue reading...
title: Youth unemployment in UK falls below 1 million

author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
description:
Minister calls for Instagram owner to extend sweeping new safeguards for young users to Britain

  • UK politics live – latest updates

  • Business live – latest updates

The UK government expects the Instagram owner Meta to roll out the same protections for children in Britain as those it agreed in the US on Wednesday, as part of a court settlement that could cost the company up to $18bn (£13bn).

Pat McFadden, Labour’s work and pensions secretary, said on Thursday that he did not want young people in the US to hav
title: UK expects Meta to match US child safety measures after $18bn settlement

author: Rachel Hall
description:
Rescue teams are searching for nearly 1,400 missing people, mostly tourists, after floods kill at least 270

  • Nepal-Tibet flash flood – latest updates

Rescue teams in Nepal are searching for at least 33 British nationals who are among those missing after flash floods ravaged its border with Tibet, killing at least 270 people.

Nearly 1,400 people are missing, most of them tourists, authorities have said, after a glacier collapse triggered devastating floods in Nepal and Tibet, roaring down valleys and razing entire villages.

Continue reading...
title: Search on for at least 33 Britons missing after flash floods in Nepal and Tibet

author: Adam Gabbatt
description:
As the US president struggles to end his Iran war, and approval ratings hit new lows, he leans on a familiar gambit

Donald Trump knows the power of an image – of himself, with everyone from Vladimir Putin and Kim Jong-un to Kim Kardashian. How about George Washington?

As the US president struggles to end his war with Iran, and with his approval ratings hitting the lowest levels of his second term, he has in recent weeks posted a series of AI-generated images of himself alongside key historical American figures.
title: AI slopper in chief: Trump turns to social media amid tough questions

author: Presented by Michael Safi; produced by George McDonagh and Alex Atack; music by Rudi Zygadlo; sound design by Brian McNamara; executive producer Joshua Kelly
description:
People are becoming convinced AI chatbots have helped them make scientific breakthroughs, cure diseases or invent new technologies. What does this reveal about a technology used by more than a billion people? A new series from The Guardian Investigates, coming soon

Continue reading...
title: Black Box: The Chatbots: a new series from The Guardian Investigates – trailer

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Ryan Mackenzie, running for re-election, is accused of ‘fabricating’ a career in the real estate industry

The Republican congressman Ryan Mackenzie has been accused of embellishing his résumé with private sector experience in real estate sales amid an acrimonious showdown over his Pennsylvania seat.

Mackenzie, who has previously been accused of lying about his age on Tinder, “was a real estate salesperson licensed in PA”, according to his LinkedIn profile, and biographies have consistently listed it has his former profession.

A woman who died in a house fire along with her seven-year-old niece has been described as “a beautiful soul”.

Natalie McDonald, 34, died along with her niece Valentina Foster, seven, in the blaze in Grangetown, near Middlesbrough, in the early hours of Wednesday.

title: Woman killed with niece in Middlesbrough house fire was ‘a beautiful soul’, says mother

Elderly Aids Ltd, which sells call-blocking devices, made 758,053 cold calls between May 2024 and February 2025

A company that made its money promising to protect elderly people from nuisance calls has been fined £190,000 for “hounding” them with hundreds of thousands of nuisance calls of its own.

The Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) said Elderly Aids Ltd, a company selling call-blocking devices, made 758,053 cold calls between May 2024 and February 2025 to try to sell its products.

description:
State government says ‘breach bail, go to jail’ laws raise risk of overcrowding in jails, while one expert warns they may lead to ‘cruel outcomes’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Queensland government’s latest law and order crackdown – subjecting some children as young as 10 to a mandatory sentence of a year behind bars – could lead to “cruel outcomes”, according to human rights lawyers.

In documents tabled with the legislation on Thursday, the government conceded its laws, dubbed “breach bail, go to jail”, would breach human rights and risk further straining the state’s overcrowded jails, youth detention centres and police watch houses.

description:
Government measures to improve resilience are not due until 2030 and July’s hack has not altered this timeline

Hundreds of Britain’s smallest power plants could remain at a higher risk to state-sponsored cyber-attacks until the 2030s despite a successful Iran-linked hack last month, it has emerged.

Officials this week briefed energy bosses on the breach, which is understood to have shut an unnamed small gas power plant for four days last month, and put the industry on alert over the growing cyber threat facing energy infrastructure.

Continue reading...
title: UK’s small power plants face continued cyber risk after Iran-linked hack

description:
Report shines light on ‘catastrophic situation’ where young people make themselves more ill to avoid losing support

Some of the most vulnerable children and young people in care are deliberately self-harming to avoid being abandoned when they get better or turn 18 and face a “cliff edge” of no further support, according to research.

Abi Booth, a psychotherapist who works with children and young people, said some were in a “catastrophic situation” in which they were hurting themselves to keep their place in therapeutic facilities.

In the UK, the youth suicide charity Papyrus can be contacted on 0800 068 4141 or email pat@papyrus-uk.org, and in the UK and Ireland Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In the US, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is at 988 or chat for suppor
title: Vulnerable children deliberately self-harming to stay in care, research finds

Lawyers claim Eman el-Shazly, from Birmingham, was detained in effort to silence her sister, a critic of Sisi regime

The UK Foreign Office has been asked to intervene to secure the release of a British-Egyptian woman who it is claimed has been arrested in Cairo because of her sister’s political activism.

Eman el-Shazly, a 45-year-old based in Birmingham, was arrested on 16 August while visiting Egypt. Her lawyers say she has been detained in an attempt to silence her sister Mona, a relentless and harsh critic of the Egyptian government on her UK-based YouTube channel.

The once world-leading producer of crude oil has plunged into an energy crisis as Kyiv targets its refineries

A sanctioned shadow fleet tanker carries oil from Nato member Turkey to a Russian Baltic port. A deal is signed for Russian oil to be processed in Kazakhstan. Fuel cargoes arrive from India via Egypt. The Kremlin pressures allies to sell it badly needed fuel.

The data points may be diverse, but they point to a single inescapable conclusion.

Rules will require hedge funds, insurers and pension firms to report all non-financial wrongdoing

The City’s largest hedge funds, insurers and pension funds are racing to prepare for sweeping rules that will stop nearly 40,000 companies from hiding bullying and harassment cases from the financial watchdog.

From the start of next month, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) will expand a crackdown on bad behaviour in the banking industry to a wider group of City investment firms and brokers.

title: City firms race to prepare for FCA crackdown on bullying and harassment

description:
Exclusive: utility company wants to draw off tens of millions of litres of water a day from Thames and replace it with treated effluent

Levels of a toxic “forever chemical” rose to 13 times the legal limit during Thames Water pilots for a controversial multimillion pound water recycling scheme that will pump millions of litres of treated sewage into the River Thames during drought.

The data from the pilots is in stark contrast to public comments from Thames Water that their water recycling project in south-west London will not harm the riverine environment.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Forever chemicals’ surge during pilot of Thames Water plan to combat drought

description:
Horticulturalists begin moving and propagating plants before the rusty and warped Palm House begins renovation – but some are too tall to save

It will be a gut-wrenching moment for the horticulturalists at Kew Gardens when some of the magnificent trees in the Palm House have to be felled.

“There are some sad moments ahead,” said Palm House manager, Will Spoelstra, who knows all the plants inside the cathedral-like greenhouse.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Sad moments ahead’: Kew Gardens to fell rare trees in race to save Victorian greenhouse

description:
Parliamentary committee welcomes fact most of 472 missing have been found but ‘extremely concerned’ for rest

Forty children who went missing from hotels housing asylum seekers in the UK have still not been found, according to a parliamentary report.

Ministers are facing calls from MPs and peers to explain what they are doing to locate the group, two of whom are believed to still be under 18. The figure emerged in a report on Thursday by the joint committee on human rights on how the social care system is failing young adults.

Continue reading...
title: Forty children reported missing from UK asylum hotels still not found

description:
The 80-seat venue at Edinburgh fringe combines sauna rituals with theatre, music, storytelling … and sweat

Tucked away behind the Summerhall arts centre is the hottest new venue at the Edinburgh fringe … quite literally. The Sauna theatre has proved popular among theatregoers at the world’s largest performing arts festival, with shows inside its purpose-built, 80-seat sauna drawing sweaty, swimwear-clad crowds.

Visitors may be forgiven for thinking the sauna is a gimmick, especially at the fringe where absurd, experimental and ludicrous performances are not uncommon. This year they include a man drinking his own urine, someone singing the same song over and over,
title: Hot ticket: UK’s first sauna theatre draws swimwear-clad audiences

author: Angelique Chrisafis in Paris
description:
Comté, beaufort and abondance makers can temporarily supplement cows’ diets as there is ‘no grass left to eat’

Strict production rules will be loosened for some of France’s most famous cheeses after drought and repeated heatwaves dried out grazing pastures, threatening the livelihoods of traditional dairy workers.

Comté, a hard cheese made from raw cows’ milk in the Jura mountains, is France’s top-selling traditional cheese, with more than 62,000 tonnes produced last year. The government announced on Wednesday that its producers would be granted a temporary change to strict rules on grazing after farmers said extreme heat had scorched their pastures, putting production at risk.
title: France to relax cheese production rules after drought takes toll on grazing land

From the 1950s to the 2020s, Kusama produced vivid paintings, sculptures and vast installations that often drew on her experience of hallucinations

Yayoi Kusama, the Japanese outsider artist who reached superstar status after decades living in a psychiatric hospital, has died aged 97.

Kusama died in a Tokyo hospital on 14 August, her studio announced in a statement on her website on Thursday.

Nepali tour operator fears 15 Australians who had been on a trekking tour near border with China have died after devastating flooding

A Nepali tour operator says he fears that 15 Australians trekking with his company in a valley ravaged by flash flooding have died.

Sagar Pandey, the founder and chief executive of Himalayan Glacier Trekking, said he has lost all contact with his tour group of 47 people, which included 15 Australians.

Busy Philipps has revealed she had a brain tumour removed, which was diagnosed shortly after her Dawson’s Creek co-star James Van Der Beek died from bowel cancer.

The 47-year-old, born Elizabeth Philipps, starred in the hit US teen drama as Audrey Liddell opposite Van Der Beek, who died in February aged 48 after being diagnosed with bowel cancer.
